feasible.reason: The proposal is sound in kind: it is a measurement campaign, not a countermeasure, and it correctly targets the one premise (HW-ASSUME-RDP2, status `cert-cited`) that the FSBL-frozen-forever story and the first-boot ceremony both lean on. The repo evidence checks out: evt-silicon-validation.md:12 says FI resistance has never been exercised on any hardware; tools/bench/ has only read-only connectivity probes and its own README gates the campaign engine (milestone 2) on the still-undecided Scaffold<->U585 coupling and crowbar drive; HW_ASSUMPTIONS.json HW-ASSUME-RDP2 has no silicon evidence and its note says no board in the project has ever been at RDP-2; issues #301/#376/#232/#236 are all OPEN; `sca-trigger` exists (secure/Cargo.toml) and on pq1 maps to PB3, which is bonded on the 48-pin part and not an LCD/SE pin. docs/security/red-teaming.md section 6.6.1 already specifies exactly the two shapes (FaultyCat EM = micro-Glitch, Scaffold voltage = Simonik) and section 3.3 binds `RDP2` to sacrificial U585s, so the proposal is really "execute the written plan" (novelty is below parity, which is fine). Nothing here needs a product hardware change, so kind=process is correct; cost L and P0 are defensible given a positive RDP-downgrade result would force a redesign and must land before the ceremony. It is NOT refuted, but several items as written are not realisable at the stated throughput/evidence level on pq1 without changes listed in corrections.
feasible.corrections: (a) Do not spend pq1 EVT units on item (1): the RDP/TZEN option-byte-loader behaviour is a die property shared by the STM32U585AII6 (iota2 dev kit) and the U585CIU6 (pq1), so burn ~$70 B-U585I-IOT02A kits to RDP-2 for the downgrade sweep and reserve pq1 silicon for board-level questions (rail topology, SE collateral). Record DBGMCU_IDCODE rev per part (HW-ASSUME-U585-REV) and confirm OEM2LOCK/OEM key absence before the lock, otherwise an apparent downgrade is uninterpretable. (b) "Fault-model-complete (voltage, clock, EM)" is wrong for this board: pq1 clocks from HSI16 x PLL1 (secure/src/hw/rcc.rs:3), there is no external clock to glitch, so clock-FI is out of the model; and red-teaming.md 13.2 explicitly refutes the F4-style "crowbar VCAP" recipe for the U5 -- the injection rail (LDO vs SMPS mode, rcc.rs:165 says the boost path is regulator-mode dependent) must first be identified on a sacrificial part with decoupling caps lifted; this is board rework on a sacrificial unit, not a product change, but the proposal should say so. ChipWhisperer-Husky is not on the bench (on-hand: Scaffold + FaultyCat + Rigol MHO934); if Husky is wanted it is a purchase, and micro-Glitch needed four coordinated faults, so a single-fault null on the TZ-config window is not reassuring and must be reported as such. (c) Item (3) is throughput-infeasible as written against real SEs: every non-successful shot with a wrong PIN charges page 124, the SE050 UserID and OPTIGA E120 (HW_PIN_CTR_LIMIT = 32 lifetime per provisioning, reset only via the admin-wipe path), so 10 shots -> brick -> `make wipe-for-wizard` + re-provision per cycle; thousands of shots need a fenced bench feature that re-arms the three counters between shots while leaving the `gated_unlock` code bytes identical to the production build (prove by diffing the symbol's disassembly across the two builds), plus `e2e-test` so PIN entry needs no buttons on the panel-less pq1 bench board. (d) Item (4): there is no feature to turn the double-compute OFF (none in secure/Cargo.toml), so an ON-vs-OFF comparison needs a new NEVER-ship fenced feature; Genet's SPHINCSplus-FA tooling targets reference SPHINCS+ parameter sets and does not run against C10 (bespoke tweakable hash/ADRS, WOTS+C target-sum, h=18 d=2) -- the grafting exploitability oracle must be re-derived for C10 (d=2 is the worst case: one faulted layer-1 WOTS leaks top-layer forgery capability fastest); at 6-14 s per sign on pq1 a "thousands of shots" sweep is days, not hours, even with sca-trigger narrowing; and the `if !ct_eq { Err }` branch at secure/src/crypto.rs:366 is itself the single-instruction target, sweep it explicitly. (e) Item (5): 1k traces is far too few to put a number on F-16. On stm32u585 the secret-seed PRF runs in the HASH peripheral (hw-sha256 is implied by the `stm32u585` feature), and the F-16 shuffle is a de-alignment countermeasure, so a fixed-vs-random t-test needs shuffle-OFF + trigger-aligned traces at >=10k (ideally 100k) to show the underlying leak, then shuffle-ON to show reduction; it needs a sense resistor inserted in the MCU supply path on a sacrificial pq1 (rail rework), and the consumption mask comparison is meaningless on pq1 because PA6 is NC (no load), so do not report a mask number from pq1 without adding a load. (f) Item (2): the FSBL crate has no `sca-trigger`; add a trigger toggle in the FSBL around filter_valid/verify_images (PB3 is free there). Fault susceptibility is binary-specific: results on the current 32 KiB bench FSBL do not transfer to the post-#540 40 KiB shipping FSBL, and the secure-firmware items (3)(4)(5) are per-release evidence, so bind each receipt to the reproducible-build hash. The only one-off results are the die-level RDP-2/TZ-config answer and the frozen final FSBL binary; everything else is recurring cost (cost is L plus recurring), or must be approximated per release with rainbow/Unicorn calibrated once against silicon. (g) Keep the EM coil local and monitor SE liveness between shots (red-teaming.md 13.3): the SE rail VDD1_3V3 is isolated from MCU VDD, which protects the SEs from crowbar but not from an adjacent EMFI coil.

Repo side: FI resistance is documented as never exercised on hardware (docs/hardware/evt-silicon-validation.md:11-12); tools/bench has only instrument probes (probe_scaffold.py = 40 lines, no glitch terms; tools/bench/bench/__init__.py:4 and README.md:26 both say the glitch campaign engine is 'next'); HW_ASSUMPTIONS.json:302-336 carries HW-ASSUME-RDP2 with falsifying_test.exists=false and procedure pointing at docs/security/red-teaming.md §6.6.1 (lines 670-690 define the two shapes); issues #301, #376, #236, #232 are all OPEN per gh; secure/Cargo.toml:644-652 defines sca-trigger and it is genuinely unwired (grep shows zero Trigger::raise() call sites outside secure/src/hw/sca_trigger.rs itself, despite that module's own header lines 27-34 claiming it fires in c10_sign_verified_with_progress / cmac_dhuk / gated_unlock). All C10/SCP03 fault sweeps under tools/sca/ are rainbow/Unicorn emulation, consistent with 'Unicorn emulation' in the threat text. Trezor side: /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware ships FI countermeasures in code (random_delays.c:184-203 wait_random with error_shutdown('(glitch)'), boardloader/main.c:356-358 volatile next_stage_addr FIH, bootloader/main.c:678-690 wipe-on-fatal, storage.c guard-bit counter) but no on-silicon glitch campaign tooling or published U5 glitch data (grep for chipwhisperer/donjon/riscure/emfi across code+docs returns nothing campaign-related; only Tropic GLITCH_DET config rows). Safe 5 / Safe 7 are STM32U5 (T3T1/T3W1/T3B1 config.mk:1) while Safe 3 attacked by Donjon is T2B1 = STM32F4 (config.mk:1; Ledger article names TRZ32F429). Ledger side: Donjon blog index lists TROPIC01 (2026-06-03), Tangem laser (2026-07-09), RP2350 (2026-09-18), Coldcard, Trezor One write-ups, and the only 'own devices' FI content is the rainbow-based simulation post (ledger.com/blog/fault-injection-simulation: simulation only, no physical results or traces published) — so 'Ledger does not publish its own [silicon campaigns]' is accurate. Ledger's 03/12/2025 article states verbatim that for the STM32U5 'no fault injection attack has been made public at the time of this writing', so the shared-assumption framing is confirmed for BOTH vendors. Sources: Bozzato/Focardi TCHES 2019 confirms F373 RDP Level-2→Level-1 with a glitch 11 µs after boot (pdf text lines 559-569); Sass USENIX'23 confirms STM32L5 as an evaluated target, four coordinated voltage faults (SAU, AHB CTRL, DUPL, PE) and the 'conceptionally similar ICs' transfer claim (pdf lines 289, 688-696, 718-735); SPHINCSplus-FA README confirms attack/evaluation/experimentation with a real ChipWhisperer-Lite + CW308 STM32F4 setup; Šimoník thesis exists at is.muni.cz/th/nysvv (Trezor-supplied STM32U5A9 boards, Husky + PicoEMP). Novelty='parity' is correct: no vendor publishes a reproducible on-silicon FI campaign with scripts+traces on its own current part, but Donjon runs equivalent campaigns on competitors, so this is matching the field's best practice rather than beyond it.
vendor-claim.corrections: (1) Šimoník '~76% PIN-check bypass' is sourced only from a 2026-03-24 it4sec Substack summary and from the repo's own HW_ASSUMPTIONS.json:336 / red-teaming.md:973-976 (which already admits the thesis numbers were not extractable); the thesis PDF at is.muni.cz/th/nysvv/thesis.pdf is session-gated (curl returned a 195-byte HTML page), so the 76% / 1.1% EMFI figures remain unverified against the primary source. Also it is a bachelor's thesis on an STM32U5A9NJ dev board (MB1829), a PIN-check software bypass, NOT an RDP downgrade or flash readout — do not let the threat line read as if a U5 RDP break exists. (2) The 'Neither Trezor nor Ledger has published a U5 data point' sentence is true but incomplete: Trezor (SatoshiLabs) SUPPLIED the two U5A9 boards for the Šimoník work, so the only public U5 glitch data point is Trezor-enabled, just not Trezor-published; and Ledger explicitly wrote (03/12/2025) that no public U5 FI attack existed and that the U5 'design explicitly takes into account' glitching — i.e. Ledger shares the same unevidenced assumption, which strengthens the rationale. (3) Donjon's Safe 3 result is an STM32F4 (TRZ32F429, T2B1) data point — voltage-glitch bypass of the MCU firmware hash/authenticity check — not a U5 one; the threat text does not claim otherwise but should say so. (4) Kraken did F205 (Trezor One) and F427 (Model T) RDP2→RDP1 in 2019/2020; Unciphered's 2023 Trezor T demo was characterised by Trezor as the same RDP-downgrade class and Unciphered disputed that — cite it as 'claimed same class', not confirmed. (5) µ-Glitch needed FOUR coordinated faults off one trigger on the L5 and spent up to 24-48 h per parameter search; the campaign design should be multi-fault-capable (Scaffold/Husky multi-glitch) or a single-fault null result on the SAU/GTZC window proves little — this caveat is already in red-teaming.md:966-972 and should carry into the proposal's 'risks'. (6) repo_evidence drift to add: secure/src/hw/sca_trigger.rs:27-34 documents call sites that do not exist (zero Trigger::raise() callers); wiring the trigger is a prerequisite step the proposal currently assumes is done. (7) Source eprint 2024/367 is Saarinen's SLotH (SLH-DSA hash-unit accelerator with a 100k-trace TVLA on the protected PRF) — it supports only item (5) TVLA-on-PRF, not any glitch/RDP claim; label it as such. (8) Ledger's Donjon blog index does not carry a Safe 3 post; the Safe 3 write-up is the ledger.com 'Why Secure Elements make a crucial difference' article (03/12/2025) plus Trezor's vulnerability page (reported 2024-11-12) — cite those URLs instead of the generic blog.
